summary: Restoring a configuration backup now marks first-run setup complete, so the setup wizard no longer reappears after the restart — a restored machine is treated as already configured, matching what the user expects after applying a backup. Previously the setup-complete flag was intentionally excluded from the backup payload (it's host-local state), which left the wizard showing again until manually skipped. backupService.Restore now writes the setup.state runtime-setting after a successful restore (best-effort; surfaced via RestoreResult.SetupCompleted). The forced first-login password change is unaffected — it's a separate login gate, not the wizard — so skipping the wizard doesn't weaken the new-machine's admin credential. Also added a server-side log line to the capacity calibrate endpoint's estimate-build failure path (5xx detail is hidden from clients) so a 'Run Calibration -> internal server error' is diagnosable from the log, and a portable procutil smoke test asserting HideWindow keeps child stdio working.
compatibility: No API/config change. RestoreResult gains setupCompleted/setupCompleteError fields (additive). Behavior change: a restore (Settings tab or first-run wizard) now sets the setup-complete flag; on a fresh install this dismisses the wizard after the post-restore restart.
